explanation: Far from the origin a polynomial is ruled entirely by its highest-power term, so y = a·xⁿ captures the whole story of its tails. Step the degree n through whole numbers: even n sends both arms the same direction, while odd n makes the arms point opposite ways. The sign of the leading coefficient a then decides which way is up — flip a negative and the whole picture turns over. The violet arrows mark which way each end heads.
bullets: Even degree: both ends agree (up–up or down–down). Odd degree: ends oppose.
a > 0 lifts the right end; a < 0 flips both ends.
Only the leading term matters for the far-left and far-right behavior.
